peer obtains the OS user from the kernel and is available only for local connections (Unix-domain sockets), while ident uses the IDENT protocol (RFC 1413) to look up the OS user from a TCP/IP connection; if ident is specified for a local connection, PostgreSQL uses peer instead.

GSSAPI authentication requires setting `krb_server_keyfile` and ensuring the postgres service principal is registered with the Kerberos KDC; it depends on Kerberos 5 infrastructure and GSSAPI support, with optional principal-to-role mapping via `pg_ident.conf`.

A role with LOGIN can authenticate and connect to the database (acting as a user), while a role without LOGIN cannot connect directly but can be used as a group to which other roles are granted membership via GRANT, allowing shared privilege management through SET ROLE or automatic INHERIT.

SET ROLE lets a role temporarily assume another role's privileges if the original role is a member of it via GRANT; SET ROLE NONE restores the original. session_user is the original login role and remains unchanged, while current_user changes to reflect the role set by SET ROLE.

pg_basebackup creates a binary copy of the entire running database cluster using the streaming replication protocol and is used to set up a new standby server, while pg_dump produces a logical backup of a single database as a SQL script or custom-format archive and is used for migrations and small-to-medium backups.
log_min_duration_statement logs any SQL statement that runs for at least the specified number of milliseconds; setting it to 0 logs every statement, producing high volume.
